citations.F1: `serialize_event` does one `SELECT ... FROM users` per event, sequentially awaited — batch this into a single `WHERE id = ANY($1)` (or join)
citations.F2: then dedupes with `if key in seen` on a plain list, which is O(n²)
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses synchronous `requests.get` ... blocking the whole asyncio event loop thread for up to 2s per uncached IP ... Fix: use an async HTTP client (httpx.AsyncClient) or move the call off the event loop.
citations.F4: `events` has no index on `(org_id, created_at)`, so the query is a sequential scan over all 4.2M rows for every call — add a composite index `events(org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` is appended to on every request and never trimmed — cap it (ring buffer / reservoir) or replace with a proper histogram.
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded dict keyed by IP, never evicted, growing forever — bound it (LRU with a max size, or a TTL)
citations.F7: re-measure endpoint p95 via the same Datadog view
citations.F8: Root cause of the 1.2-1.6s DB time ... Root cause of the remaining 5-10s and of the healthz outage: `lookup_geo` uses synchronous `requests.get`
citations.F9: Don't ship the on-call proposal as-is — it doesn't touch the root causes and the pool math is dangerous. ... 16 workers × pool max 50 × 6 pods = up to 4,800 connections — that alone can take down Postgres
citations.F11: the mobile client never sends `since`, so the handler computes it as `now() - 30d` fresh on every call (sub-second precision) — almost never a cache hit
